forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Waverley reports £2.9m General Fund and £3.0m housing account underspends for 2025/26
news_drafts.lead:
Waverley Borough Council ended 2025/26 with a £2.9m underspend on its General Fund, the account that pays for services funded by council tax and business rates. Its housing revenue account, the ring-fenced account for council housing paid for by rents, underspent by £3.0m. The figures are in the annual report of the council's external auditor, which went to the Audit & Risk Committee on 16 November 2026.

The General Fund underspend compares with £1.7m in 2024/25, and the housing account's with £1.02m. The General Fund result includes £2.4m of staffing savings and £1.7m of treasury income.

The auditor's report says: "While the General Fund and HRA outturn positions were favourable, these were influenced by non-recurring factors rather than the delivery of recurring savings." It says both results were driven by non-recurring factors.
news_drafts.paper_title: Appendix 4 - Waverley BC Auditor's Annual Report (AAR) 2025-26

news_drafts.headline: Waverley opened 2026/27 with a £7.3m general fund deficit, forecast to narrow to £4.5m by year-end
news_drafts.lead:
Waverley Borough Council began the 2026/27 financial year with its main day-to-day account (the general fund) £7.3m in deficit, and forecasts it will end the year £4.5m in deficit, according to budget papers for its Executive committee on 6 October. The council puts the £2.8m improvement down to £1.1m of budget movements and £1.7m from commitments, money already set aside for specific purposes.

The papers show a similar pattern in the money set aside against business rates, the tax on commercial property. The reserve for timing differences on government grants and for spreading the cost of a deficit started the year £3.75m in deficit. Budget movements of £2.67m are forecast to bring that to £1.08m in deficit. A separate reserve covering risks to the council's medium-term financial plan, its multi-year forecast of spending against income, is forecast at minus £665k, after £197k of budget movements and £280k of commitments.

Two income lines are forecast below budget. Planning land charges, the fees for property searches, are expected to bring in £345,565 against a budget of £406,070, a shortfall of £60,505 or 14.9%. Commercial Waverley Training Services is forecast at £368,965 against £406,635, a shortfall of £37,670 or 8.5%.

findings.paper_title: Draft Supplementary Estimate Agency Report WBC
findings.headline: The paper links continued agency cover to the ongoing final accounts and audit process, budget setting, and Local Government Reorganisation workstreams.
findings.detail: The paper states that covering posts through temporary agency arrangements avoids service disruption and maintains business continuity during these activities. It lists financial reporting, audit and budget-setting activities among the risks if approval is not given.
findings.matters: A finance director would see that staffing gaps are being tied directly to the final accounts and audit timetable, which matters for any council at the same point in the cycle.
findings.quote: This is particularly important given the ongoing final accounts and audit process, budget setting activities, Local Government Reorganisation workstreams and delivery of statutory services.

findings.paper_title: Draft Supplementary Estimate Agency Report WBC
findings.headline: The paper states that the financial pressure is expected to diminish if external recruitment approval is granted.
findings.detail: The paper says agency arrangements would be reduced on approval of external recruitment. Until then, expenditure is forecast to exceed existing staffing budgets during the period agency cover is needed.
findings.matters: The paper links the cost directly to a single decision, the outstanding recruitment approval, which a finance director elsewhere could look for in similar reorganisation delegations.
findings.quote: Should approval for external recruitment subsequently be granted, agency arrangements will be reduced and the financial pressure is expected to diminish.

findings.paper_title: Draft Supplementary Estimate Agency Report WBC
findings.headline: Costs are for 2026/27 only with no ongoing revenue implications, within Executive authority for £50,000 to £250,000
findings.detail: The paper says the supplementary estimate is subject to there being no ongoing revenue implications for future years. Agency arrangements continue until 31 March 2027 or until recruitment approvals are received, whichever is sooner.
findings.matters: A finance director would check whether a supplementary estimate of this size is limited to one year, which shapes how other councils treat similar agency overspends.
findings.figures: £50,000 to £250,000 (Executive authority range); £209,393 (estimate sought); 31 March 2027 (end date)
findings.quote: These costs are for 2026/27 only and there are no on going revenue implications as a result of this request.

findings.paper_title: Draft Supplementary Estimate Agency Report WBC
findings.headline: The paper gives an annualised additional cost of £502k for Guildford.
findings.detail: The paper states that the supplementary estimate does not represent the total cost of temporary staffing arrangements. It gives the annualised figure as a separate number for the other council sharing the posts.
findings.matters: An annualised figure indicates the scale of the cost if agency arrangements continue beyond the 2026/27 period covered by this request.
findings.figures: £502k annualised additional cost (as stated for Guildford)
findings.quote: The annualised cost would be a additional £502k for Guilford.

findings.paper_title: Draft Supplementary Estimate Agency Report WBC
findings.headline: The total additional agency cost for 1 November 2026 to 31 March 2027 is £418,784, funded £397,181 from the General Fund via the LGR Reserve and £21,603 from the HRA via HRA Working Balances.
findings.detail: The paper splits the total cost equally between Waverley and Guildford under the agreed cost-sharing arrangement. The General Fund element is charged to the Local Government Reorganisation Reserve and the HRA element to HRA Working Balances.
findings.matters: Drawing on a Local Government Reorganisation Reserve for operating staffing costs is a funding choice finance officers at other councils in transition will compare.
findings.figures: £418,784 (total); £397,181 (General Fund total); £198,591 (General Fund Waverley share, from LGR Reserve); £21,603 (HRA total); £10,802 (HRA Waverley share, from HRA Working Balance)
findings.quote: The General Fund element will be funded from the Local Government Reorganisation Reserve and the HRA element from HRA Working Balances.
